text:
The Red Wings trailed in the third period and still left Edmonton with the extra point. Dylan Larkin tied it at 3-3 with 1:17 left in regulation, and Detroit won the shootout 4-3 when Lucas Raymond scored in the first round and Michal Postava stopped all three Oilers shooters, Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins among them.

Detroit's second period is why this didn't feel like a fluke. In expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of shots, the Red Wings outplayed Edmonton 1.92 to 0.86 in that period. Viktor Arvidsson, drafted 112th overall by Nashville in 2014 out of Skelleftea, scored on the power play and also had a 64% look stopped by Tristan Jarry. Over the full game our numbers say Detroit deserved to win 57% of the time, meaning it won that share of simulated replays of every shot. Edmonton was better in the third (1.07 to 0.51), and Colton Dach, a 62nd overall pick in 2021 who played 48 AHL games in Rockford two seasons ago, tipped in the 3-2 goal with 3:28 left. Even Emmitt Finnie's equalizer, on just a 4% chance, fit the pattern of a team that kept getting chances and finally got paid.

The facts we have don't include either team's record or streak, so the result stands on its own: a road team that was dominant in one period and dangerous in the last, against a home team that led twice and couldn't close either time.
